China state-backed capital piles into AI champion DeepSeek as AI, robot IPOs face curbs
sum: [DigitalToday reporter Jinju Hong] Chinese artificial intelligence (AI) company DeepSeek has raised $15.8 billion in new investment and is seeking a listing on the Shanghai stock market. A total of 31 new investors joined the round, and many are believed to be linked to Chinese state-owned capital.

On Nov. 19, local time, blockchain media outlet Cryptopolitan reported that the round was the largest venture investment raised by China’s AI industry so far. DeepSeek’s valuation was put at about 615.5 billion yuan. DeepSeek nearly doubled the size from what it originally planned during the fundraising process. The impact reflected stronger demand to secure large-scale computing resources as U.S. export controls pushed up black-market prices for Nvidia Blackwell B300 servers.

Registration filings show that shareholder platform Hangzhou Chengyan has newly joined DeepSeek’s operating entity. This also confirmed the close of the second funding round. Hangzhou Chengyan’s committed capital increased to about 3.44 billion yuan from 6,000 yuan, and DeepSeek’s registered capital also expanded to about 19.9 million yuan, up about 21.1%.

By investor composition, a Tencent affiliate secured the largest stake at 9.57%. Three funds linked to battery company CATL held the same proportion. China Mobile’s investment arm and CITIC Securities each held 7.65%, and a fund linked to Monolith Management accounted for 7.17%. Vivo, Midea, Geely, Xiaohongshu, Meituan and NetEase were also included in the investor list.

A notable point is the share of state-owned capital. State investors provided 27% of the round’s funding. That is a sharp increase from about 2% in the first round in April. China’s 60 billion yuan national AI fund invested about 980 million yuan in the first round. At that time, DeepSeek’s valuation was about 350 billion yuan.

DeepSeek is preparing for an IPO on Shanghai’s STAR Market, the science and technology board. It selected CITIC Securities as lead underwriter and aims to enter the listing process before year-end. Founder Liang Wenfeng (량원펑) stepped down from his status as a direct partner of Hangzhou Chengyan, but he maintains control by holding 99% of the company that manages the platform.

items.t: All Three Major US Stock Indexes Fall Over 2%; Anthropic Rises 17% in Debut; Wave of Buybacks and Stake Increases Sweeps China's A-Shares
sum: Overnight, US stocks suffered a broad selloff, with all three major indexes closing down more than 2%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 2.19%, the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.25% and the S&P 500 lost 2.02%. Leading technology stocks were almost uniformly lower: Amazon fell 3.87%, Google dropped 3.46%, Nvidia declined 3.30%, Meta lost 3.27%, Tesla fell 2.43%, Microsoft slipped 1.78% and Apple edged down 0.92%. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index closed down 2.41%, with AMD plunging 7.72%, while chip stocks such as Applied Materials and Micron Technology also fell. Popular Chinese ADRs came under pressure as well, with the Nasdaq Golden Dragon China Index closing down 1.86%: NetEase tumbled 11.39%, Baidu fell 4.09%, and NIO and XPeng dropped more than 3%, while Pinduoduo bucked the trend to surge 11.04%.

Amid the weak market, the trading debut of AI company Anthropic was the biggest bright spot. The company closed up 17.07% at $97.17 per share on its first day on the Nasdaq, after rising as much as 38.7% intraday, lifting its market value to $1.27 trillion. The IPO raised about $81.3 billion, surpassing SpaceX's $75 billion in June this year and setting a record for the largest IPO ever. Meanwhile, international precious metals prices fell sharply, with spot gold briefly dropping below the $3,630 mark intraday, down more than 2%; spot silver fell 4.3% to $43.2 an ounce. Europe's three major indexes also all closed lower, with Germany's DAX down 0.85%, France's CAC 40 down 0.65% and the UK's FTSE 100 down 0.87%. Asia-Pacific markets extended the weakness in early trading, with Japan's Nikkei 225 opening 1.5% lower and South Korea's KOSPI falling 4.08%.

China's A-share market, by contrast, kicked off a fresh wave of buybacks and stake increases, with a number of listed companies密集 disclosing buyback plans on the evening of Nov. 19. CXMT (688825.SS) raised the upper limit of its buyback amount from the original plan to between CNY 2.5 billion and CNY 5 billion (approximately $375 million to approximately $750.1 million), at a maximum price of CNY 63.78 per share, with a market value of about CNY 2.55 trillion.

DeepSeek's 10-Billion-Yuan Financing Round Officially Finalized: How Did Perfect World, Hengdian, and Huace Group Secure Spots in the Landmark Investment Deal
sum: On November 17, Hangzhou DeepSeek completed industrial and commercial change registration. Qichacha data shows that it added a new shareholder, Hangzhou Chengyan Enterprise Management Consulting Partnership, marking the second round of financing officially landed at the industrial and commercial administration level.

According to public reports tracked by Entertainment Capital Theory, this round of financing raised about 1.055 trillion yuan (158 billion U.S. dollars), with a post-money valuation of about 6.155 trillion yuan (860 billion U.S. dollars), setting a new single-round financing record for Chinese AI companies. As a shareholding platform, Chengyan added 31 new partners at one time, with a registered capital contribution of 3.439 billion yuan. It now has a total of 32 partners, holding 17.26% of DeepSeek's shares.

Among the 32 names, in addition to industrial and state-owned capital representatives such as CATL, China Mobile, CITIC Securities, China Life, SMIC, ChangXin Memory, Midea and vivo, there are also six names of entertainment and content platforms: Tencent, NetEase, Xiaohongshu, Hengdian, Bilibili, Perfect World, and the more circuitous Huace.

Especially the fact that mid-sized entertainment companies like Perfect World, Hengdian and Huace can squeeze into this list alongside many industry giants is in itself a signal worthy of attention. Could it be that DeepSeek will also enter the AI video field and embark on the multi-modal path in the future?

The 32 partners of Chengyan who took shares in the second round add up to exactly 100% of the capital contribution ratio. The author of Entertainment Capital Theory reversed calculated how much each party actually paid by multiplying the ratio by the 1.055 trillion yuan raised in this round: Tencent's 9.5653% stake corresponds to about 100.9 billion yuan, which is consistent with the 100 billion yuan figure in public reports; the Lisi Capital related entity's 7.1740% stake corresponds to about 75.7 billion yuan; Boyu Capital's 3.3479% stake corresponds to about 35.3 billion yuan.
According to this standard, the "entry tickets" for the entertainment sector are divided into three tiers.

items.t: HK unveils unified drone platform to take LAE from pilots to scale
sum: Hong Kong opened a demonstration center on Tuesday where government departments will share drone resources through a single management platform, signaling a shift towards industrialized, large-scale applications in the city’s fledgling low-altitude economy.

The Hong Kong Productivity Council (HKPC) and the government’s Working Group on Developing Low-altitude Economy jointly opened the Unmanned Aircraft Operation Management Demonstration Centre, which features a centralized operating system designed to serve as a digital foundation for a smart city.

Sunny Tan, chairman of the HKPC, said the center is “more than a technology exhibition platform”. “It represents an important step in advancing drone applications from a single pilot towards shared, platform-based and large-scale development,” he added.

Deputy Financial Secretary Michael Wong Wai-lun, who also heads the working group, reaffirmed the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region government’s commitment to developing the low-altitude economy and positioning the city as a hub for its applications.
He said the government is working closely with stakeholders across society to draw on their expertise and integrate low-altitude technologies into daily life to improve public services.
More than 20 government departments have joined the project, exploring applications including public facilities monitoring, pollution prevention and climate data analysis.
“By closely partnering with various societal stakeholders, the government is pooling collective wisdom to integrate low-altitude tech into daily life for better public service,” he said.

Rechargeable Phone Ring Holder Market To 2035: Smartphone Stand Demand Drives Growth - News and Statistics
sum: According to the latest IndexBox report on the global Rechargeable Phone Ring Holder market, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture.

The global rechargeable phone ring holder market is transitioning from a niche gadget to a mainstream smartphone accessory, with a clear split between high-volume commodity products and premium, benefit-driven brands. Demand is bifurcated: a price-sensitive mass market seeks basic grip and stand functionality, while a growing premium cohort prioritizes design, brand association, fast charging, and multi-functional features. Channel strategy is critical, as success hinges on mastering e-commerce platforms and navigating retail shelf-space dynamics. Private-label penetration is rising, pressuring margins for lower-tier brands.

The supply chain remains concentrated in East Asia, with differentiation achieved through design, branding, and channel agility. Pricing follows a three-tier ladder: value, mainstream, and premium. Geographic roles are distinct: North America and Western Europe are brand-building and premiumization markets; East Asia is the manufacturing and innovation hub; Southeast Asia and Latin America offer high-growth, price-competitive opportunities. Future growth will be driven by portfolio premiumization, share capture from non-rechargeable holders, and managing customer acquisition costs in saturated digital channels.
The category faces risks from smartphone design integration, battery regulations, and margin erosion from platform-driven price transparency.

The baseline scenario for the rechargeable phone ring holder market anticipates steady growth through 2035, with a CAGR of 5.8% from 2026 to 2035. This outlook is supported by the increasing adoption of smartphones as primary devices for entertainment, navigation, and productivity, which drives demand for accessories that enhance usability. The market is expected to benefit from the rising popularity of wireless charging, as rechargeable ring holders can integrate charging capabilities, offering convenience and differentiation. Premiumization is a key trend, with consumers willing to pay more for design, brand, and advanced features.

sum: China Mobile has delivered a powerful long term share price run, yet the recent pullback raises a fresh question about whether today's valuation still lines up with its earnings strength. For anyone looking at telecoms as an income and stability anchor in a portfolio, the key puzzle is how much of China Mobile's current price can be pinned to its profit power rather than sentiment.
Over the past 5 years the stock has returned 141.9%. This now puts a lot of weight on whether those gains rest on a durable earnings base.
The group runs a capital intensive network business. Cash flow, depreciation and ongoing investment all feed directly into how much of its earnings can realistically be paid out or reinvested.
The stock's next move may depend on whether China Mobile's current price looks well supported by its earnings when set against a Fair Ratio benchmark.

If you want a second reference point while you assess China Mobile against its earnings power, you can apply the same approach to a broader set of companies using the 195 high quality undervalued stocks.

The P/E ratio suits China Mobile because investors often look at it as an earnings and dividend workhorse rather than a high growth story. On this measure, the stock trades on about 11.6x earnings, which sits below the wireless telecom industry average of roughly 14.8x and also under the broader peer group at about 24.3x. That marks a clear gap between what the market currently pays for China Mobile's profits and what it pays for telecom earnings elsewhere.

The tailored Fair Ratio, which blends factors such as the group's margins, growth profile, market size and risk, points to a level close to where China Mobile now trades. The current P/E sits only slightly above that modelled anchor, so the share price does not screen as especially expensive or particularly cheap on this single metric. Anyone weighing the stock now is really judging whether the quality and resilience of its earnings justify a multiple that is a discount to sector averages but broadly aligned with its own Fair Ratio. sum: China Tower Corporation Limited, together with its subsidiaries, provides telecommunication tower infrastructure services in the People's Republic of China. The company engages in the construction, maintenance, and operation of base station ancillary facilities, such as telecommunications towers and public network coverage in high-speed railway tunnels and subways, large-scale indoor distributed antenna systems, and integrated digital infrastructure service. It also offers towers, and shelters or cabinets; and ancillary equipment to TSPs to facilitate the operating of their telecommunications equipment. In addition, the company provides maintenance services, including monitoring equipment operation, routine inspection, device breakdown handling, property upkeep, working environment protection, and operation analysis services. Further, it offers power access, batteries, or back up power generation to the customers' telecommunications equipment; and indoor distributed antenna systems connecting telecommunication equipment, enabling them to receive and send indoor mobile telecommunication network signals, as well as mobile telecommunication network signals covering large venues, buildings, and tunnels. Additionally, the company provides backup power services for standby emergency power supply to corporate customers; battery exchange services to replaceable batteries to individual customers; battery recharge services to corporate and individual customers; and trans-sector site application and information services, as well as integrated information, power generation, and energy storage services. The company was formerly known as China Communications Facilities Services Corporation Limited and changed its name to China Tower Corporation Limited in September 2014. The company was incorporated in 2014 and is headquartered in Beijing, China.

Nvidia CEO Exit Saga Fuels Rally in Chinese AI Chip Stocks; Domestic Share Seen Near 90% in 2026
sum: On Nov. 12, the AI chip sector on China's A-share market bucked the broader trend. Enflame Technology rose more than 13% intraday, MetaX gained nearly 9%, and Moore Threads and Cambricon each climbed more than 8%, with Intellifusion, Biren Technology (Hong Kong-listed) and Hygon Information Technology following higher. The immediate trigger for the rally was fresh developments in the question of whether Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang will stay or go.

According to the Shanghai Securities News, foreign media cited people familiar with the matter as saying that Nvidia's board is preparing to remove Huang, and could hold a meeting as early as Thursday local time to decide his fate. Huang had previously acknowledged an extramarital affair, prompting the Nvidia board to launch an independent investigation; subsequent reports said he had an affair with Kimberly Powell, the company's vice president of healthcare. Under Nvidia's code of conduct, employees must "avoid situations that create a conflict of interest," including "personal relationships." The report also said Nvidia is working with an outside firm to identify potential new CEO candidates and is considering appointing an interim CEO before a broader search.

In response to the rumors, Zhang Guobin, founder and CEO of EET China, laid out three lines of observation in an interview. On the litigation front, a shareholder class action was filed after the close on Nov. 9 against Nvidia and Huang personally, with the core allegations centering on four statements the company made about Megaspeed. It is the second securities class action against Huang, and together with a $5.5 million penalty from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) in 2022, the disclosure records of both Huang and the company are being re-examined. On the congressional front, three House committees have asked Huang to attend a closed-door briefing on Nov. 18 on issues including Megaspeed's procurement and chip flows. On the corporate governance front, the board could, under the code of conduct, remove him at the most severe end of the scale, but several Silicon Valley figures judge that he faces no immediate risk of departure — Huang has an enormous influence on Nvidia's operations and share price, and the company has no clear No.

Zhipu Launches HK$4 Billion Share Buyback as Chairman Liu Debing Leads the Charge
sum: Hong Kong-listed Chinese large-model developer Zhipu (02513.HK) announced the launch of an H-share repurchase program with a cap of HK$4 billion (approximately $509.8 million). The news sent the stock gapping higher in early trading on the 11th, surging more than 6% intraday to a high of HK$512.

According to a voluntary announcement Zhipu released on the evening of the 10th, the buyback stems from a share repurchase proposal by Chairman Liu Debing. The company will buy back its own H-shares on the open market at opportune times under the general mandate granted at its annual shareholders' meeting on June 22, 2026. The total repurchase amount is capped at HK$4 billion, with a second threshold: the number of shares bought back may not exceed 1% of the total issued shares as of the announcement date. Both limits must be satisfied simultaneously.

Zhipu said in the announcement that the repurchase plan primarily demonstrates management's confidence in the group's long-term business outlook and prospects, as well as its commitment to enhancing shareholder value. In execution, the board will take into account the company's financial position, working capital needs and business development to ensure sufficient financial resources remain for daily operations and growth. The company also cautioned that this is only a repurchase intention, and the timing, price and actual number of shares bought back will be at the board's discretion based on market conditions, with no guarantee of full execution.

The announcement also stated that the board and authorized persons will not exercise the repurchase mandate in a way that would trigger a mandatory offer obligation under Rule 26 of the Takeovers Code, or reduce the proportion of H-shares held by public shareholders below the minimum threshold required by the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong. The mandate is valid until the conclusion of the company's 2026 annual shareholders' meeting, or the date shareholders revoke or amend the mandate by special resolution, whichever occurs earlier.
Market participants analyzed that the buying wave reflects not only the buyback theme but also expectations of a valuation recovery for the large-model sector.

sum: Nvidia shares fell 4.3 percent in New York on Monday despite a Wall Street rally in tech shares after the chipmaker's board opened an independent inquiry into whether Chief Executive Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. Huang, 63, admitted and apologized for an extramarital affair with a Singapore-based businesswoman now suspected of gathering intelligence for China. US President Donald Trump later told a press briefing that the FBI is investigating the affair but Huang has assured him he had had no idea she might be a spy. China's Foreign Ministry dismissed the espionage allegation as a baseless smear.

The fate of Taiwan-born Huang – co-founder of Nvidia 33 years ago, mastermind of its growth into the world's most valuable chip company and a sort of an AI rock star – isn't clear. If he were forced out, there's no clear successor. The company's directors said they have "confidence in Jensen" and "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised." Elon Musk and other industry moguls have come out in support of Huang.

The 31st UN Climate Change Conference has begun in Turkey following a year that has produced record high temperatures and increasing natural disasters blamed on a warming planet. Representatives from about 190 countries are debating how to address a climate crisis that shows little signs of slowing. The world's biggest emitter of greenhouse gases won't be attending. The US pulled out of global climate agreements after President Trump took office nearly two years ago and began dismantling pollution control policies. Past summits of the UN group have focused on setting limits on harmful emissions, though implementation has fallen short of goals. The climate debate is complicated by continuing friction between rich and poor countries over who pays for the impact of the climate crisis. Africa, in particular, which has faced prolonged droughts and destructive flooding, says it contributes little to greenhouse gas emissions and should receive funds to cope with the fallout. And low-lying island nations in the Pacific Ocean that are particularly susceptible to rising sea levels want aid.

China Mobile Partners with Zhipu: Chinese-Made Computing Power Fully Integrated with GLM Models
sum: China Mobile (00941.HK) and Zhipu (02513.HK) have formally signed a cooperation agreement, under which the two sides will pursue deep collaboration in three major areas: Chinese-made computing power, Large Language Model services, and the commercialization of artificial intelligence. Zhipu's GLM series models will also be integrated into China Mobile's model service system.

Under the arrangement, the two parties will carry out joint innovation on adaptation of Chinese-made computing power, improvements in Token production efficiency, development of AI Coding products, and industry applications such as finance and government affairs, with the goal of accelerating the large-scale deployment of Large Language Models in key industries. From a technology-chain perspective, the cooperation spans the complete chain from underlying computing power supply and model services to commercial distribution.

Zhipu believes that allying with China Mobile will help connect the upstream and downstream segments of the industrial chain, improve model inference efficiency, and expand the scale of GLM model usage and commercialization channels, driving Large Language Models from independent technological innovation toward large-scale industrial application. Overseas reports noted that the GLM models will be connected to China Mobile's Mobile Cloud model-as-a-service platform, a move that also echoes the direction of China's official AI policy at the current stage, which emphasizes Chinese-made computing power and application deployment.
The market reacted positively to the news, with Zhipu's shares rising more than 5% in early trading to HK$448.4 (approximately NT$1,900).

items.t: Is VNET Group (VNET) Undervalued After Earnings Growth Met Leverage Concerns?
sum: VNET Group (VNET) has drawn fresh attention after its latest quarter showed 14.2% revenue growth and a 133.3% rise in earnings per share, set against a balance sheet carrying net debt of 6.8x EBITDA.

VNET Group’s share price has fallen sharply despite the latest earnings jump, with a 30 day share price return down 41.5% and the year to date share price return down 65.4%. The 5 year total shareholder return has declined 82.4%, pointing to fading momentum and a market that continues to price in balance sheet risk even as revenue growth and large scale data center contracts draw fresh interest.

Spot opportunities with similar pressure points by scanning our hand-picked 39 high quality undervalued stocks. These ideas combine growth stories with compressed valuations and balance sheets that investors are still questioning.

For VNET Group, the gap between growing data center revenue and a shrinking share price raises a simple tension: Is the latest slide signaling deeper business issues, or has sentiment pushed the valuation too far down?

VNET Group last closed at $3.16, while the most followed narrative anchors on a fair value of $12.71. This frames the recent share price slide against a much higher long term expectation based on growth and risk assumptions.

Strong, sustained growth in wholesale data center capacity utilization and demand, especially for AI-driven workloads in regions like Greater Beijing and Yangtze River Delta, positions VNET to benefit from the accelerating digitalization and increased AI/cloud adoption across China, directly supporting higher future revenues and occupancy rates.
Still, the VNET Group story leans heavily on high leverage and large 2025 CapEx plans, so any refinancing hiccup or weaker wholesale demand could quickly reset expectations.

items.t: Ambani’s Jio soars 21% on Mumbai debut
sum: MUMBAI: Shares of billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Jio Platforms ​soared 21% in their Mumbai debut yesterday, making it India's second-largest company ‌by market capitalisation, valued at about US$131.5 billion (RM537 billion). Jio, whose telecoms ​business serves more than 530 million customers, is backed by Meta Platforms and Alphabet's Google. Its user numbers are second only to China Mobile on the basis of single-country subscribers. The listing, the ​first for the Reliance conglomerate in two decades, furthers Ambani's plan to turn Reliance from an oil-and-chemicals conglomerate ‌into an “everything company” spanning ​consumer products and technology. The listing ceremony was ​attended by Mukesh Ambani, Akash Ambani, his eldest son and Jio's managing ​director, and his wife Nita Ambani. Ambani's other children Isha and Anant Ambani also attended. The stock opened at 1,358 rupees a share, compared with its 1,119-rupee offer price. Jio's market capitalisation overtook Bharti Airtel and HDFC Bank, becoming the second-largest Indian firm by that metric. Several brokerages see a potential upside for the Jio stock, but they flagged competition, heavy capital spending and changes in India's telecom rules, including those related to spectrum, licensing and fees. “Jio has had a strong debut even despite geopolitical issues and turbulent market conditions … the revenues and earnings will lead the ‌stock here onwards,“ said Kranthi Bathini, equity strategist at WealthMills Securities. The Ambani family rang the IPO bell on stage at the National Stock Exchange in Mumbai. An emotional Mukesh ​Ambani was seen in tears as Anant traced Reliance's and Jio's legacies and journey in a ​speech ​at the ceremony. Major Indian newspapers yesterday carried front-page ads from Reliance ‌Jio, saying “Thank ​you, India.” India has become the world's busiest IPO market this year in terms of the number of deals, with 246 listings so far, though it ranked fourth by money raised at US$13.5 billion, behind the US, mainland China and ​Hong Kong, LSEG data showed. – Reuters

Watching the performance of US AI-related stocks tonight, I found myself wondering if this marks the start of panic selling. In particular, some semiconductor and data center stocks dropped more than 10%, which is indeed concerning.

For years, I’ve frequently reminded everyone about risk management, position sizing, and maintaining a healthy investment mindset. This isn’t just empty talk; I genuinely don’t want to see too many friends suffer significant losses of their principal due to overexposure or excessive leverage when the market suddenly plunges.

As I get older, my investment strategy has changed quite a bit.Compared to before, I now try to minimize exposure to high-leverage products. In the US market, I prefer Apple (AAPL.US).$Apple (AAPL.US)$ These are large companies with relatively mature businesses and stable cash flows. Of course, even Apple can decline; no stock is guaranteed to be safe.

I’m not sharing this to be cynical, but rather to help you avoid common pitfalls through my investment experience. There will always be opportunities in the market, but if you lose too much of your principal, it’s extremely difficult to recover.

China Mobile Stock Technicals: Gains 1.91% on Friday, Testing Key Resistance
sum: On October 30, 2026: price 80.00 HKD, trend sideways, RSI 56.4, support 77.10, resistance 81.00. technical analysis of china mobile stock.

China Mobile’s shares rose 1.91% to HKD 80.00 in Friday’s Hong Kong session, October 30, as trading volume surged and the MACD histogram turned positive. The move is notable because it was about 1.4 times the stock’s average daily trading range, but the broader trend remains sideways and on-balance volume fell, leaving a gap between price strength and underlying buying participation.

That makes China Mobile a useful read on whether a burst of activity can push the shares through nearby resistance—or whether the rally runs into supply. The stock gained 3.76% over five days, while its one-month advance was a more modest 0.69%, according to the supplied market data.

China Mobile ended above its 20-day moving average of HKD 79.14, a short-term positive, but that average remained below the 50-day average of HKD 79.39. The 20-day average fell 0.22% over five days, so the latest price rise has not yet changed the underlying direction of that trend measure. No new moving-average crossover was recorded.

The shares were positioned at 74% of their 20-day trading range, between support at HKD 77.10 and resistance at HKD 81.00. That places price closer to the upper boundary, where a sustained break could signal that buyers are overcoming resistance. The three-month high of HKD 84.95 remains a more distant reference point; the three-month low was HKD 77.00.
As shown in the chart, the shares are above the 20-day average but still face resistance near the top of the recent range.

Momentum indicators leaned mildly constructive without showing an extreme. The RSI was 56.4, in neutral territory; the Relative Strength Index measures the pace of recent price moves, and this reading does not indicate that the stock is stretched in either direction. Stochastic %K at 64.5 stood above %D at 39.8, also within neutral territory, suggesting improving short-term momentum rather than a decisive breakout signal.

The company had a price to earnings ratio of 10.94 and a market capitalization of HKD 1,611.6 billion on October 21, 2026. China Mobile's financial year ends on December 31, while its investor-relations page identifies HKEX stock code 941 and the Hong Kong listing.
